Egg prices before the spikes

Freeze the forecast before each documented outbreak period, then compare it with what happened.

These are forecasts of how earlier price patterns might continue. They do not identify prices in a world without HPAI. Feed costs, inflation, demand, policy and other shocks also enter the gaps. The 2024 origin already includes earlier HPAI waves and higher prices.

Design

Original 544 monthly prices only, January 1980–April 2025. Each origin uses all earlier history; six disjoint 12-month rolling validation blocks select among the nine existing R models. Selection and fitting stop at the origin. Forecasts remain frozen for 12 months, with no actual-price updates. All structures and coefficients are re-estimated using the available history. The 80%/95% bands are model forecast intervals, not confidence intervals for a causal effect.

Episode boundaries come from the sources below, not an algorithm searching for the largest residuals. This is a retrospective, exploratory study. Seven months are observed for the October 2024–September 2025 forecast; the five remaining actual prices are unavailable and are not filled. Different event horizons must not be ranked as comparable accuracy tests.

Earlier-origin sensitivity

origin_sensitivity.csv moves each origin back one and three months. The model is selected again using only complete validation folds ending before that earlier origin (five folds). Targets stay on the same event months. Results show dependence on origin and method choice; they do not create a causal control group.

Reproduce

Run Rscript analysis/spike_counterfactual.R or use analysis/spike_counterfactual.ipynb. CSVs retain all 324 forecasts, observed gaps, per-fold validation predictions, selection scores, earlier-origin sensitivity and calendar audits. frozen_models.rds and sessionInfo.txt retain fitted models and runtime details.
